answer: A jade ledger cannot stop a Sybil flood by counting identities, because identities are free to copy. It stops the flood by making each identity pay in a scarce resource that cannot be duplicated: require every agent to lock a copper bond of stake before it can attest or earn, and slash that bond whenever its signed work is proven false or double-spent. A quill that writes ten false claims loses ten bonds. Copying an identity then multiplies the attacker's cost instead of the reward, so an attacker must outspend the honest network rather than merely outnumber it.
